refinedPriorNodes.label: SessionStore
refinedPriorNodes.refinement: Session CLOSED remains a semantic continuity boundary: it blocks new SessionItems and new DelegationEnvelopes but is not itself an authorization revocation primitive for already-created delivery effect identities.

refinedPriorNodes.label: PolicyDecisionStore
refinedPriorNodes.refinement: R9 PolicyDecision remains the durable route-time policy snapshot. R15 does not reinterpret that historical decision as sufficient current authority for the first external delivery effect.

refinedPriorNodes.label: TransferAwareDeliveryCoordinator
refinedPriorNodes.refinement: R15 wraps the existing R12 transfer-aware delivery path with an effect-time authorization gate; quiescence, replay-safety, claim-transfer and same-binding recovery ownership remain unchanged.

discoveredNodes.label: EffectAuthorizationDecisionStore
discoveredNodes.reason: A current authorization observation must be durably frozen to one exact immutable TransportBinding/effect identity before the first external send attempt, separately from route-time policy.

discoveredNodes.label: EffectAuthorizationCoordinator
discoveredNodes.reason: The first external delivery effect requires a fresh PolicyAdapter observation and fail-closed behavior when no current policy authority is configured.

discoveredNodes.label: EffectAuthorizedDeliveryCoordinator
discoveredNodes.reason: Existing receipts replay without inventing a new effect authorization, while a new external send is blocked until the exact Binding has an allowed effect authorization decision.

discoveredNodes.label: AgentServiceR15
discoveredNodes.reason: R15 adds effect-time current local policy authorization over the frozen R14 delivery identity without rewriting R9-R14 historical semantics.

flow: first R15 delivery attempt -> N88 current PolicyAdapter observation
N87 freeze allow/deny for exact binding/effect identity
deny or missing policy authority -> fail closed before provider send
allow -> N89 delegates to existing N72 TransferAwareDeliveryCoordinator
existing DeliveryReceipt -> local replay without a new provider effect or authorization event
same binding/effect recovery -> reuse frozen N87 decision
new/failover Binding -> new N87 effect authorization required
authorityLaws: SemanticSession is continuity state, not an authorization token or implicit revocation authority.

Closing a Session prevents new SessionItems and new DelegationEnvelopes but does not retroactively erase an already-created DelegationEnvelope, TransportBinding or frozen effect authorization decision.
Route-time PolicyDecision establishes historical route admissibility only; it is not sufficient current authority for the first external delivery effect.
Every new external delivery effect identity must obtain one current PolicyAdapter observation immediately before crossing the local provider-effect boundary.
Missing effect-time PolicyAdapter fails closed before adapter.send.
Allowed and denied effect authorization decisions are both durable and bound to exactly one TransportBinding.
A denied frozen effect identity is not silently re-evaluated into allow; a later newly authorized action requires a new effect identity/Binding.
Once an external effect identity has an allowed decision, recovery of that exact identity reuses the frozen decision rather than turning policy drift into a second logical effect.
An existing durable DeliveryReceipt is historical evidence of an already-observed provider admission and does not require a new authorization event merely to be replayed locally.
R15 does not weaken R12 quiescence/replay-safety/claim-transfer rules, R11 semantic-completion rules, or R14 credential currentness checks.
Remote providers remain responsible for their own authentication and authorization on each protocol operation; R15 is a local authority gate, not a substitute for provider authorization.

R15 does not claim that Session closure can never be an input to policy. A PolicyAdapter may deny current effect authorization based on Session or other revocation state; that decision belongs to the policy authority.

standardsBasis.use: Authorization checks apply at protocol-operation boundaries; scope, validity and revocation semantics remain implementation/credential-issuer defined rather than being implied by task/session continuity.
The protocol core is stateless and each request is self-describing, supporting the separation of Ordivon semantic continuity from transport authorization state.

nonClaims: R15 does not define a universal revocation service.
R15 does not make provider effects exactly-once.
R15 does not retroactively cancel an effect that may already have crossed the provider boundary.
R15 does not equate Session CLOSED with policy denial.
R15 does not replace credential expiry/currentness checks or remote-provider authorization.
